..Partly cloudy skies across southeast Arizona this 
afternoon with a few cloud build-ups especially across the higher 
terrain south and east of Tucson. Just a few showers so far on radar 
for these locales and these should diminish after sunset. A fairly 
similar forecast for Friday but with a slick uptick in mid level 
moisture we'll see a few more cloud build-ups with a slight chance 
(10% to 20%) of showers and thunderstorms once again mainly from 
Tucson area south and eastward. Rain amounts will be mainly less 
than 0.10" so not really impactful though can't rule out a few 
stronger wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph near any showers.   

For this weekend, all eyes will be focused on the trough of low 
pressure to the west along with Tropical Storm Rachel which will 
recurve towards northern Baja Mexico. The latest forecast from the 
National Hurricane Center shows Rachel moving onshore as a 50 kt 
Tropical Storm across northern Baja late Saturday night and then 
becoming post-tropical as it moves into southwest Arizona Sunday 
morning. The track has shifted a bit to the east over the past 24 
hour which does put some potential for higher wind gusts from Tucson 
westward. The ECMWF and its ensembles are particularly strong for 
wind gusts, depicting a widespread area in excess of 50 mph over the 
T.O. Nation and western Pima County on Sunday with 35-50 mph 
elsewhere. The GFS/GEFS and official forecast are a bit more muted 
for winds but certainly the potential is there for an upward 
adjustment in our official wind forecast which has wind gusts of 35-
50 mph. Later shifts will likely need to hoist wind headlines for 
Sunday. It is not unprecedented that tropical origin systems can 
result in gusty winds across the desert southwest. While not exactly 
the same setup, an example of this was Hurricane Nora in 1997 that 
came into north central Baja as a hurricane and resulted in 
sustained tropical storm winds in Yuma as it raced north. 

Outside the wind threat on Sunday, the other main impact from this 
system will be rainfall. Moisture will be on the increase on 
Saturday ahead of Rachel and given enough solar insolation, we 
expect scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop 
Saturday afternoon and continuing into Saturday evening. A few of 
these thunderstorms may be strong with gusty winds in excess of 40 
mph and locally heavy rain with localized rain amounts 0.50" to 1 
inch in the strongest storms. Otherwise, for Saturday, precipitation 
amounts will generally range from about 0.05" to 0.35" for those 
locales that see rain. 

On Sunday, rain will hinge on 2 factors...the remnants of Rachel and 
precipitation along its immediate track and outside of that, how 
much atmospheric destabilization we see for shower and thunderstorms 
activity especially from Tucson eastward. This part of the forecast 
still has quite a bit of uncertainty with is but any thunderstorms 
that do develop have the potential to be strong to severe given the 
strong wind-shear that will be present.

For Monday and Tuesday, the main factor for our weather will be the 
trough axis to our west. There will still be another area of forcing 
and lift as a cold front moves through the region from late Monday 
into Tuesday and that is likely to bring us more shower activity and 
potentially a few thunderstorms as well. Winds will remain gusty on 
Monday but certainly not nearly as strong as Sunday. Drier air will 
then move in Wednesday with any lingering precipitation chances 
Wednesday to the east of Tucson. 

Storm total precipitation amounts of 0.25" to 1 inch still looks 
reasonable for most valley locations with 1 to 2 inches in the 
mountains. The lower end of these amounts will tend to be over 
Cochise County with the highest amounts north to west of Tucson. 
Most of the precipitation is expected Saturday and Sunday and while 
isolated flash flooding may occur with any stronger thunderstorms 
this weekend, we're not expecting widespread flash flooding 
concerns. 

Above normal temperatures through Friday will give way to near 
normal temperatures on Saturday, then an extended period of below 
normal temperatures will occur Sunday through the middle of next 
week.
